clue.text: Sound of derision at game with the French

parts.note: whist is a card game for four players
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Jeers ring out at a match involving the French team.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle from the crowd is a common way to show scorn or mockery.

clue.text: Man is identified who carried out the robbery

parts.note: he is a man
taken as written
the man is identified by name, as Ted

explanation.surface: The man who committed the robbery has been named.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the start as 'he is Ted': the man is identified by name.
explanation.definitionFit: To heist is to rob, especially in an armed hold-up, so heisted means robbed.

clue.text: Plant end of herbaceous border

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its last letter is used
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A gardener places a plant at the end of the herbaceous border.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Places drawn roughly to scale

indicators.note: drawn roughly suggests a rough sketch, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A map shows places drawn approximately to scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to place or site it, so locates matches the verb places.

clue.text: Gave voice to song returning after drink

parts.note: sang is past tense of sing, to give voice

indicators.note: returning means the word for song is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone sang a tune again after having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch made from red wine and fruit, a classic summer beverage.

clue.text: Having got up article about increase in pay

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a rise is a pay increase in British usage

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a pay rise, written by someone just out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A rise is the British term for a raise in salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Arisen is the past participle of arise, to get up or stand.

clue.text: Old John allows bits of armour

parts.note: John of Gaunt was a 14th-century English prince, 'time-honour'd Lancaster' in Shakespeare
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A historical John permits pieces of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, is the 'Old John' of Shakespeare's Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauntlets are armoured gloves worn by knights.

clue.text: Got lit up on gin mixed with vermouth by journalist

indicators.note: mixed suggests a cocktail, and here signals the letters of gin are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, the spirit's name as written
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk on gin with vermouth alongside a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Lit up is slang for drunk, which the surface exploits; the definition takes it literally as set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignited means caught fire or set alight, the literal sense of lit up.

clue.text: Girl with one unfinished poem, a sign of celebrations

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: verse means a poem
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A girl writes part of a poem, a token of celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries are yearly commemorations of an event, observed as festivities.

clue.text: Helpful nature

definitions.meaning: first meaning: considerate and generous to others

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase about character, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means benevolent, while the noun means a sort or category, as nature does in 'things of that nature'.

clue.text: Union acting without a revolution going on

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means the letter for a is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: the fodder, both words as written
the single letter as written

explanation.surface: A trade union keeps working without staging an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something continuing is carrying on or proceeding, the sense of going on.

clue.text: Give evidence about a time trial

parts.note: taken as written
a test is a trial or examination

explanation.surface: A witness speaks about a time trial, as in a cycling race against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true.

clue.text: Fish with t-tiny problem over sense of self

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: a problem with the letters means they are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the stammered word gives its letters as written, extra T included

explanation.surface: A tiny stammer over a fish leads to an identity crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in t-tiny is not decoration: it supplies the second T the fodder needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity is who a person is, their individual character or selfhood.

clue.text: Letter opener

definitions.meaning: a piece of post, not an alphabet character
not a paper knife but the person who opens the envelope

explanation.walkthrough: A letter opener is normally a knife; here it is the recipient who opens the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person to whom mail is directed, so they are the one who opens it.

clue.text: He tells stories about con artist — possibly true!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of true could be arranged another way

parts.note: the fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A storyteller spins a yarn about a fraudster, perhaps true.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes.

clue.text: Way of fighting Livingstone and the party

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A politician and his party are described by their combative approach.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone is a British left-wing politician, formerly Mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: One who receives protection from the outside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dealer in stolen goods, a receiver
second meaning: a barrier around a property

explanation.walkthrough: In criminal slang a receiver handles stolen goods, which is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a trader in stolen property and a boundary barrier that keeps intruders out.

clue.text: And in France renal failure is constant

parts.note: et is French for and

indicators.note: failure means the letters of renal break down into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, as written; renal means of the kidneys

explanation.surface: A French doctor notes that kidney failure is persistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting and unchanging, a synonym of perpetual.

clue.text: They value animals around Ross

parts.note: asses are donkeys

indicators.note: around means the letters of Ross are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the man's name supplies its letters as written

explanation.surface: Donkeys gathered round a man called Ross are being valued.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessors are people who estimate the worth of property for tax or insurance.

clue.text: Build lavatory frame straight up

parts.note: to erect is to build

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters form the frame

explanation.surface: A builder puts up a toilet frame vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: Erectly means in an upright, vertical position.

clue.text: Withdraw the first old fashioned driver to pull up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up means reading from the bottom upwards
first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: only its opening letter is taken
a carter drove a horse and cart

explanation.surface: A vintage carriage driver pulls up and backs away.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or recant, the same as to withdraw a statement.

clue.text: Of one mind about the elderly going out

indicators.note: going out means the word for the elderly sits outside the other piece

parts.note: the aged are old people
re means concerning

explanation.surface: People agree about old folk taking a trip out.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed means in accord, with everyone sharing the same view.

clue.text: What everyone becomes after twelve

definitions.meaning: sounds like a riddle about a change that comes to all
suggests midnight on the clock, but means after the twelfth birthday

explanation.walkthrough: Twelve suggests the clock; it is an age, and thirteen starts a new stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The years from thirteen to nineteen are the 'teens', so a thirteen-year-old is a youth of that bracket.

clue.text: Just quality in actors' union

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fairness, the quality of being just
second meaning: the British trade union for performers

explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the name of the UK trade union for actors and performers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means impartial fairness and is also the name of the performers' trade union.

clue.text: Superior drug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: higher in rank or position
second meaning: slang for a stimulant

explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective the word means higher; as slang it is a stimulant such as amphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means higher-ranking and is also slang for a stimulant pill.

clue.text: Prior enacted ten changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of these two words are reshuffled

parts.note: the fodder, both words as written

explanation.surface: A former ruling once passed ten amendments to the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedent means preceding in time or order, a formal synonym of earlier.

clue.text: Writer's work for which fee is about a pound

indicators.note: is about means the fee word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: pay is a fee or wage
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A writer is paid roughly a pound for a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a drama written by a playwright, a dramatist's creation.

clue.text: Hitler came back, taking in one state then another

indicators.note: taking in means the reversed name encloses the other piece
came back means the name is reversed

parts.note: Adolf was Hitler's first name
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A dictator returns, swallowing one state after another.
explanation.walkthrough: One state is the abbreviation inside; another state is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is a US state, just as Rhode Island is, so it is another one.

clue.text: Water for rodent in Hyde Park

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: only Hyde, the park's name, is used
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone asks for water for a rodent living in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydrate is to supply water, so as a verb it means to water.
